Guide

The modern data-science stack.

A map of how I work, from a fresh laptop to a running pipeline. Each stop has a short overview of my current setup, and the posts that go deeper will be attached to it.

1

Stop 1

Set your computer up.

I am a terminal maximalist: the editor, the file manager, the git client and the data viewer all live in the terminal, so the same setup works on a laptop, a Linux box and a phone. Neovim is the editor, just gives every project the same commands, tv is my one fuzzy finder, and lazygit, yazi and VisiData cover git, files and data. A computer at home that is always on runs the long jobs, Tailscale connects all my devices and Blink puts the terminal on my phone, so data science works from anywhere.

2

Stop 2

Coding in 2026 (with agents).

Coding agents do the typing, and I keep the decisions. uv is the cleanest way to manage Python, for me and for the agents: one tool for versions, environments and dependencies. A global CLAUDE.md carries my conventions to every project, skills package the repeatable jobs, and OpenSpec turns an idea into a plan before any code is written. herdr keeps every agent in one view, and a focus timer I built stops me from vibing on too many projects at once. All of it lives in a dotfiles repository, so a new machine gets the same setup with one clone.

3

Stop 3

How to analyse data.

I start with a look at the data and end with a document. VisiData is my spreadsheet in the terminal, far better than Excel and extensible in Python. DuckDB is my favourite tool: SQL straight on CSV, Parquet and JSON files, and one-file databases for whole projects. marimo gives me reactive notebooks with SQL cells that I can open remotely from any device, and Quarto turns the results into reports, papers and slides, at work and in academia. On the teaching side, my Big Data course for R is here too.

Posts for this stop

4

Stop 4

How to bring this to production.

Production starts with a pipeline that knows what is outdated: I began with targets in R and Snakemake in Python and now use DVC, with dvcat as its terminal UI I built. git carries the code, and I tried jj but it does not work with DVC. A daily job runs on Google Cloud as a container on Cloud Run, scheduled by Cloud Scheduler and released with one just recipe, so nothing depends on my laptop.
